rounds.text: Eyantra Ventures Ltd presents a concerning financial profile characterized by severe cash flow instability and deteriorating capital efficiency. The company reported a negative operating cash flow of Rs -11.57 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -17.27 Cr in March 2026 [E24, E25], with operating cash flow representing a staggering -2,576% of operating profit [E26]. This disconnect between reported earnings and actual cash generation is compounded by a significant increase in borrowings, which surged to Rs 16.46 Cr from Rs 0.86 Cr in the prior year [E29]. Furthermore, the company’s profitability metrics remain deeply negative, with an ROE of -16.4% and an ROCE of -8.4% [E11, E12], both of which significantly underperform their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Market sentiment reflects these fundamental weaknesses, as evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 1 against the Nifty 500 and a stock price that remains below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E35, E36]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong sales growth of 188% [E13] and a notable improvement in quarterly operating margins [E20]. Despite these top-line gains, the stock’s valuation remains stretched at 5.08x book value compared to a sector benchmark of 1.56x [E6], suggesting that the market is pricing in a recovery that the current cash-burning reality does not yet support [E42].
